items.q: A 4-year-old child presents with extreme cutaneous sun sensitivity, marked freckling and erythema after minimal sunlight exposure, dry atrophic skin, and multiple basal cell carcinomas on the face. What repair pathway is deficient?
items.exp: Xeroderma pigmentosum is caused by autosomal recessive mutations in any of eight NER genes (XPA through XPG, and XPV). Inability to excise UV-induced thymine dimers leads to accelerated mutagenesis and 1000-fold skin cancer risk.
r: Correct. Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair of UV damage.
Incorrect. BER removes small deaminated bases.
Incorrect. MMR defects cause Lynch syndrome.
Incorrect. NHEJ defects cause radiosensitivity and SCID.

items.q: What specific chemical lesion is produced in DNA following absorption of ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation, requiring nucleotide excision repair for removal?
o: Depurination of guanine forming an AP site
items.exp: UV radiation induces photochemical crosslinking between adjacent pyrimidine bases (thymine or cytosine) on the same strand, forming covalent cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers and 6,4-photoproducts that distort the double helix.
r: Correct. UV radiation produces cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers that distort the DNA helix.
Incorrect. Ionizing radiation (X-rays) causes double-strand breaks.
Incorrect. Spontaneous thermal hydrolysis deaminates cytosine to uracil.
Incorrect. Spontaneous acid hydrolysis causes depurination.

items.q: Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer, HNPCC) is an autosomal dominant cancer predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in which DNA repair system?
o: DNA mismatch repair (MMR: MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS2)
items.exp: Lynch syndrome is caused by mutations in mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2). Inability to correct post-replicative slippage errors causes microsatellite instability (MSI-H) and early colorectal/endometrial cancers.
r: Correct. Mismatch repair gene mutations cause Lynch syndrome and microsatellite instability.
Incorrect. NER defects cause xeroderma pigmentosum.
Incorrect. Homologous recombination defects cause BRCA-associated breast/ovarian cancer.
Incorrect. BER defects cause MUTYH polyposis.

items.q: In base excision repair (BER), what is the first enzyme that recognizes an aberrant, damaged base (such as deaminated cytosine forming uracil in DNA) and cleaves the N-glycosidic bond?
items.exp: DNA glycosylases recognize specific damaged or deaminated bases and cleave the N-glycosidic bond between the base and deoxyribose, creating an apurinic or apyrimidinic (AP) site for subsequent AP endonuclease cleavage.
r: Correct. DNA glycosylase cleaves the N-glycosidic bond to create an AP site.
Incorrect. AP endonuclease nicks the phosphodiester backbone at the AP site (second step).
Incorrect. DNA polymerase fills the single-nucleotide gap.
Incorrect. DNA ligase seals the nick.

items.q: Ataxia-telangiectasia is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative and immunodeficiency disorder caused by mutations in ATM. What DNA damage response kinase does ATM encode?
o: A serine/threonine kinase that detects double-strand DNA breaks and phosphorylates p53 and CHK2
A DNA polymerase that bypasses pyrimidine dimers
items.exp: ATM encodes a serine/threonine kinase activated by double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs). ATM phosphorylates p53, CHK2, and BRCA1 to arrest the cell cycle and mobilize homologous recombination repair.
r: Correct. ATM is a master kinase sensing double-strand breaks and activating p53 and cell cycle checkpoints.
Incorrect. Translesion polymerases bypass dimers.
Incorrect. Topoisomerases relieve torsional strain.
Incorrect. MutL homologues are mismatch endonucleases.

items.q: Which high-fidelity repair pathway repairs double-strand DNA breaks during the late S and G2 phases of the cell cycle by using the undamaged sister chromatid as a template?
o: Homologous recombination (HR, mediated by BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51)
items.exp: Homologous recombination utilizes the identical sister chromatid available in S/G2 phase to guide error-free repair of double-strand breaks. BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 are central effectors.
r: Correct. Homologous recombination uses the sister chromatid for error-free double-strand break repair.
Incorrect. Non-homologous end joining ligates ends without a template and is error-prone.
Incorrect. BER repairs single-base lesions.
Incorrect. NER repairs bulky adducts on single strands.

items.q: Olaparib is a PARP (poly-ADP-ribose polymerase) inhibitor. Why does olaparib selectively kill breast and ovarian cancer cells harboring BRCA1 or BRCA2 germline mutations (synthetic lethality)?
o: Inhibiting PARP blocks single-strand base excision repair; accumulated breaks collapse replication forks into double-strand breaks, which BRCA-deficient cells cannot repair
PARP inhibitors directly bind and mutate the p53 tumor suppressor
PARP inhibitors prevent topoisomerase I relaxation of DNA
PARP inhibitors directly activate caspase-9 in all cells

items.q: Non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repairs double-strand DNA breaks throughout the cell cycle, including G1 phase. What protein complex binds the exposed broken DNA ends to recruit DNA-PKcs and Artemis?
items.exp: The Ku70/Ku80 ring-shaped heterodimer encircles duplex DNA ends at double-strand breaks, protecting them from degradation and recruiting DNA-PKcs and Artemis for end processing before ligation by DNA ligase IV.
r: Correct. Ku70/Ku80 recognizes and binds exposed DNA ends in NHEJ.
Incorrect. MSH2/6 recognizes mismatches in MMR.
Incorrect. XPC recognizes bulky adducts in NER.
Incorrect. Uracil-DNA glycosylase recognizes uracil in BER.

items.q: What intrinsic enzymatic activity of replicative DNA polymerases delta and epsilon allows immediate excision of mispaired nucleotides during active replication fork progression?
items.exp: High-fidelity replicative polymerases (delta and epsilon) possess 3'->5' exonuclease proofreading activity. When a mispaired base is inserted, the polymerase pauses, shifts the terminal nucleotide to the exonuclease active site, excises it, and resumes synthesis.
r: Correct. 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading excises newly inserted mispaired bases.
Incorrect. 5' to 3' exonuclease removes RNA primers (Pol I in bacteria, FEN1 in humans).
Incorrect. Endonucleases cut internally.
Incorrect. AP lyases cleave at AP sites.

items.q: Fanconi anemia is an autosomal recessive genomic instability syndrome characterized by bone marrow failure, cafe-au-lait spots, thumb/radial ray hypoplasia, and acute myeloid leukemia. What specific type of DNA damage repair is defective?
o: Interstrand DNA crosslink repair (FA core complex / FANC pathway)
items.exp: Fanconi anemia results from mutations in the FANC genes (FANCA, FANCC, FANCD2, etc.), which coordinate the cellular response to interstrand DNA crosslinks (ICLs) caused by endogenous aldehydes and crosslinking agents like mitomycin C.
r: Correct. Fanconi anemia impairs interstrand DNA crosslink repair.
Incorrect. BER is intact.
Incorrect. FEN1 primer removal is intact.
Incorrect. Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome.
